findings.charge: The catalog carries four of the six keys of the live G20 v1 class object. The dropped slashJoiner holds a normative rule whose text appears nowhere in the artifact — that the eight surfaces are 'not eight live-cell members and not eight invented corpus-class ids' — and that rule is the one governing exactly what a catalog does.
evidence: Live G20 v1 namedCorpusClasses[0] carries six keys: id, memberVerbatim, slashJoiner, surfacesInOrder, exactByteIntent, passProperty. The catalog's class carries id, memberVerbatim, exactByteIntentVerbatim and passPropertyVerbatim, plus two additions of its own. slashJoiner and surfacesInOrder are not carried.

Live slashJoiner reads: 'human/JSON/SARIF/doctor/fault/config/progress/log stays one slash-joined surface set. The eight surfaces are cells of this one corpus class, not eight live-cell members and not eight invented corpus-class ids.'

Tested whether the rule survives elsewhere in the artifact by substring: 'not eight live-cell members' is absent, and 'invented corpus-class ids' is absent. Unlike the surfaces themselves, the prohibition is reproduced nowhere.

The immediately preceding sibling in this same catalog series, g22-named-corpus-catalog.v1, does carry its equivalent field as slashJoinerVerbatim, and both catalogs describe themselves with the identical whatIsAuthored wording naming only memberVerbatim, exactByteIntent and passProperty. So the series' own practice is to carry the slashJoiner, met once and missed here.
findings.whyThisIsNotPedantry: A catalog's product is a faithful record of the corpus class, and a later fixture-authoring cycle will read this file as that record. What it would not learn from this file is that the eight surfaces must remain cells of one class and must not become eight coined corpus-class ids — the precise constraint aimed at the artifact type doing the reading. Carrying a rule matters most when the rule governs the reader.
whyNotABlocker: Nothing false is asserted. whatIsAuthored declares the catalog quotes memberVerbatim, exactByteIntent and passProperty, and that is exactly what it quotes, so there is no overstated completeness claim.
The rule is satisfied in fact: the catalog has one class whose id is == equal to the live id, so no surface is split out and no id is coined.

surfacesInOrder, the second dropped key, is recoverable verbatim — the eight surfaces in order appear inside the carried exactByteIntent as '{human, JSON, SARIF, doctor, fault, config, progress, log}' — so its omission costs nothing and is not charged.
The one-class structure is also inferable from the carried text, which speaks of cells 'per surface in the slash-joined set'.
findings.consistencyWithThisReviewersPriorVerdict: On g22-named-corpus-catalog.v1 I accepted partly because all five keys of that class object were carried, calling completeness there 'structural rather than a matter of judgement'. On the same artifact I declined to require the sibling top-level namedCorpusNote, reasoning that the catalog's job is the class object. That drew the line at the class-object boundary; this omission falls inside it. Applying the same line in both directions is what produces a finding here and none there.
findings.whatWouldLandIt: Carry the live slashJoiner as slashJoinerVerbatim in classes[0], in the shape the G22 sibling already uses. Carrying surfacesInOrder as well would match the source object exactly, though its content is already recoverable.

verdictStatement: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Most of this is clean and I want that recorded: both equality tests the dispatch names pass by ==, with exactByteIntent equal at 1401 characters and passProperty at 398, and namedCorpusNotAuthored, the class id and memberVerbatim are equal too; all 11 cited path/digest pairs measure equal with zero mismatches; recordedInputs.HEAD agrees with the top-level head and live HEAD; closure is structurally unavailable because the artifact carries no closure-style field, and the pinned sdk-leftover-join still holds both obligations at leftoverDesign true; no SDK API, framework, envelope or D9 value appears; no id is coined, which is the failure mode a catalog is most prone to; and the subject did not move. It falls on fidelity inside the class object. Live G20 v1's class carries six keys and the catalog carries four. The dropped slashJoiner holds the rule that the eight surfaces are 'not eight live-cell members and not eight invented corpus-class ids', and substring tests confirm that prohibition is reproduced nowhere else in the file — while the other dropped key, surfacesInOrder, is recoverable from the carried text and is not charged. This is a SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker because nothing false is asserted, whatIsAuthored accurately describes what it quotes, and the rule is satisfied in fact. But the G22 catalog I accepted immediately before this one carries its equivalent field under an identical self-description, and my acceptance there rested on the class object being complete; the same line applied here yields a finding.
